name: map
title: Map
about: The world, drawn from Natural Earth's country shapes in the house style: a globe or a flat map, with every tool working on both. Drag to turn the globe or to pan the map (sideways, the flat world rolls round without end), pinch or tap twice to zoom. It can colour the sea by warmth, colour countries or bands of latitude from a table, light up countries, and show points, markers (a turning hurricane among them), great-circle routes, smooth tracks and arrows that draw themselves along, and the names of oceans, seas and continents. In a scene its camera glides softly, takes an angle, follows a storm or lets the world turn. A tap reports the place, whether it is land, and which country. The preset globe is this part with projection globe and no finger zooming.

projection.about: How the world is laid out. globe: a ball, turned by dragging. equal-earth: a flat map where every country keeps its true size (the default flat map). natural-earth: a flat map with rounder corners, sizes nearly true. mercator: the familiar web map, from 60 S to 84 N, which swells countries toward the poles (Greenland looks as big as Africa).

style.about: day: blue sea, green land. warmth: the sea coloured by surface temperature, warmest near the equator (a simplified northern late summer). muted: grey, for a map that isn't the point. political: every country in one of four colours, no two neighbours the same, like a political map.

spin.about: free: drag to turn the globe or pan the map, and it carries on a little when let go. auto: turns slowly by itself (a flat map rolls sideways), and can still be dragged. locked: stays where it is put, with no dragging or zooming by finger; taps still work.

labels.about: countries: the names of the bigger countries in view, and the name of a tapped country.

tap.about: What a tap does. country: lifts the country tapped. pin: drops a pin where the finger lands. none: nothing shows, though the tap is still reported.

view.about: Where it faces at the start: [longitude, latitude]. On a flat map the longitude runs down the middle, and the latitude counts once zoomed in.

zoom.about: How close it starts. 1 shows the whole globe, or the whole flat world; 8 is close in.

pinch.about: Pinch, or tap twice, to zoom in and out (up to 8 times). Off, two quick taps are just two taps.

equator.about: Draws the equator as a dotted line, with its name. Dotted lines (the equator, a band's edges) are always drawn over the sea and the land.

borders.about: Draws the borders between countries. Off, the land is one piece (in political, the colours alone tell the countries apart).

spinTo.about: Turns to face a place: [longitude, latitude], a country's name, or a named ocean, sea or continent. On a flat map it pans there. A soft glide of about a second unless told; 0 is at once. A move begun while another is under way carries on from its speed.

zoomTo.about: Zooms, softly: to a level (1 the whole world, 8 close in), to a country (it fills about half the view), or to [longitude, latitude] or a named place (centred there, at level 3).

camera.about: One camera move: where it faces, how close, and on a globe its angle and heading, all on one soft glide (1.6 seconds unless told). angle 0 looks straight down; toward 1 the globe is seen from low down, its horizon curving across the top of the picture with the place in front (once zoomed in to 2 or more). heading turns the picture so another way is up (degrees; 0 is north up). A flat map has no angle.

follow.about: The camera follows the newest track's head (a storm riding it) and keeps it in the middle, catching up over about seconds (1 unless told). false stops following. Any other camera move stops it too.

drift.about: The world turns by itself, degrees a second, easing to that speed over seconds: positive is the Earth's own way, west to east. 0 stops it. A scene uses it to keep a wide shot alive.

highlight.about: Fills these countries with a colour (gold unless told).

colourBy.about: Colours the map from a table. Countries: { "Brazil": 59, "France": 31 }. Bands of latitude, south negative: [[0, 10, 28], [10, 20, 27]], drawn over the sea. Numbers run along the ramp (heat: the sea warmth's navy to orange; green; blue) from the lowest to the highest, or across range [low, high] when given, so a series of tables can share one scale; a colour's name or #rrggbb is used as it is. A new table replaces the last.

band.about: Shades the sea at the latitudes from..to degrees, north and south of the equator both, with dotted edges drawn over the land too.

parallel.about: A dotted line along a latitude (south negative), with its name if given: the equator, a tropic, 5 degrees north.

label.about: Writes a place's name on the map: an ocean or a sea (pale blue spaced capitals), a continent or a country (white). It sits where that place is in view, nearest the middle, and fades in; false takes it away. For a scene: name an ocean or a continent while the line it's said in needs it.

point.about: A dot at a place, with a label if given: in a scene the label is built (a dot, a leader line, a pill unrolling with the words).

marker.about: A ring, a pin, or a hurricane (the Disc drawing) turning the way it would there: counterclockwise north of the equator, clockwise south of it. A hurricane's size follows grow. In a scene a hurricane stays still and thin streaks circle it the way it turns.

arc.about: A route along the great circle between two places, the shortest way over the Earth, drawing itself in (gold unless told), named by label if given ("" for none). It bends the way it should on the globe and on every flat map. dotted draws it as dots: the way something was aimed, beside the way it really went (a flow).

flow.about: An arrow along a smooth curve through places, drawing itself in over seconds (1.4 unless told): a wind, a current, air being bent. Cyan unless told; named by label if given, beside its middle. In a scene, once drawn, bright dashes keep running along it the way it goes, so a wind is seen blowing.

spiral.about: Air rushing in toward a place from four sides, as arrows: with bend 0 each is aimed straight at it; toward 1 each bends the way the Earth's turning bends it there (to its right north of the equator, to its left south of it), so it misses the middle and swirls round it, counterclockwise in the north and clockwise in the south. The bend is the Earth's own: strong far from the equator, gone on it, so at the equator the arrows stay straight. Called again at the same place, the bend glides to the new one over seconds (1.4 unless told). size: how far out the arrows start, in degrees (9 unless told).

winds.about: The world's wind belts blowing near the surface, as pale streaks streaming the way the wind goes: the trade winds (from the equator to about 30 degrees), the westerlies (30 to 60) and the polar easterlies (60 to the poles), north and south of the equator both. bend: 0 is how they would blow if the Earth stood still (straight toward the equator in the trades and polar winds, toward the pole in the westerlies), 1 how they really blow, swung by the Earth's turning (the trades and polar winds from the east, the westerlies from the west); called again, the bend glides there over seconds (1.4 unless told), so a scene can show the swing happening. names: each belt's name as a built label on the side facing you. none takes them away.

turning.about: The ground's own speed as the Earth turns, west to east: gold arrows along the latitudes, every 15 degrees, each the distance its ground goes in the same time, so they're long at the equator and short near the poles, dashes running along them; labels names the speeds (1,670 km/h at the equator, 1,450 at 30 degrees, 835 at 60). both: south of the equator too. false takes them away.

cells.about: The loops of air that circle between the equator and the poles (the circulation cells), drawn on a globe's right-hand edge in a thin layer of air (its thickness exaggerated, and said so): the Hadley cell rises at the equator under a tall cloud, flows toward the pole high up, sinks near 30 degrees and flows back along the ground; the Ferrel cell between 30 and 60 turns the other way, like a gear; the polar cell sinks at the pole and flows back toward the equator. Each is four arrows drawn in turn as progress goes from 0 to 1 (all of it unless told), gliding over seconds, and named once mostly drawn. south: the loops south of the equator too, mirrored. Best on a globe facing the equator, moved aside with frame; a flat map doesn't draw them. none takes them away.

frame.about: Moves a globe off the middle of the picture, x and y as shares of the picture's width and height (0, 0 is the middle; -0.3 is well to the left), gliding there (1.6 seconds unless told): room beside it for the loops on its edge. A flat map stays put.

sign.about: A sign standing on the world at a place: its pole rises at a steady speed and its board springs open with a word or a number (High, Low, +2 C). Called again at the same place with new words, its board pops again. Pink unless told. No text: it goes.

track.about: A path through places, joined by one smooth curve with no corners, drawn from its start as far as progress (0 to 1, all of it unless told), with a marker riding its head if given: a storm moving along its track, or an arrowhead. Called again with the same path, it moves that track on, gliding over seconds if given and carrying on from the speed it had, so a scene can move one storm along by steps without it stopping between them.

clear.about: Takes away every highlight, table, band, parallel, label, point, marker, route, track, spiral, key and pin, and lets go of the selected country, fading them out over seconds (half a second in a scene unless told; at once elsewhere). what: only that kind (the old winds before new ones blow, say: flows; or winds, the belts, the ground's speed and the loops of air; or signs); all unless told. Where it faces and how close stay as they are.

style.about: Changes the map's style, the old one fading into the new over seconds (1 unless told): turn to warmth when the sea's warmth starts to matter.

key.about: A key to the map's colours along its top, while its style has one: in warmth, a bar from the coolest sea to the warmest, labelled Cool and Warm. false takes it away.

grow.about: Every hurricane on the map, marker or riding a track, glides to this size (1 as drawn, 0.5 half, 1.6 bigger): a storm strengthening or dying away.

tapped.about: A tap on the map. country is null on the sea.

settled.about: It came to rest after being dragged, flicked, pinched, turned by spinTo or zoomed by zoomTo.

zoomed.about: Its zoom changed, once the change is done.

turned.about: The same moment as settled, under the name the stage 1 globe used.

selected.about: The country tapped last, with tap set to country; null if none.

tapped.about: Where the last tap landed, whatever tap is set to; null before any.

centre.about: The [longitude, latitude] in the middle: facing you on a globe.

zoom.about: How close it is: 1 is the whole world.

needs.weight: About 170 KB of shapes and scripts, kept on the phone, and six small modules. One canvas; the map itself is drawn onto a picture kept aside and redrawn only while it turns, pans or zooms, with each shape projected once per view. A turning hurricane or a moving track redraws only itself. Shapes for bands, warmth, tables and the four colours are made once, never per frame.
